scenario.fault_family: access port in wrong VLAN (misdirected prompt)
scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #8044: PC5 in Campus 1 lost its default gateway (172.16.10.254) while
PC6/PC7/PC8 on the same access switch are fine. PC5 still has link. The team
thinks switch4 -- the upstream switch that trunks Campus 1 VLANs toward mswitch0
-- must be dropping PC5's VLAN on its trunk. Please confirm the switch4 trunk
fault and identify which VLAN it is dropping.

injection.action: move PC5's access port (eth2) from br_vlan10 to br_vlan1
injection.command:
ip link set eth2 nomaster
  ip link set eth2 master br_vlan1 2>/dev/null || (ip link add br_vlan1 type bridge; ip link set br_vlan1 up; ip link set eth2 master br_vlan1)

post_inject_check.command: bridge link show | grep eth2 | grep -c br_vlan10

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath4-switch1-pc5-wrong-vlan: switch1's eth2 (the
access port for PC5) was moved out of br_vlan10 into br_vlan1, the unused default
VLAN. PC5 still sends untagged frames expecting VLAN 10 semantics, but switch1 now
bridges them into VLAN 1 -- an L2 broadcast domain with no router attached -- so
ARP for the gateway gets no reply. Other hosts on br_vlan10 (PC6/PC7/PC8) are
unaffected.

The TWIST: the ticket blames switch4's trunk. switch4 is HEALTHY -- its trunk is
carrying VLAN 10 normally, which is exactly why PC6/PC7/PC8 (also in VLAN 10, on
the same path through switch4) still reach 172.16.10.254. If switch4 were dropping
VLAN 10, ALL of those PCs would fail, not just PC5. The single-host blast radius
is the decisive tell: a trunk dropping a VLAN is a shared failure; only a
per-port (access-port) change can break exactly one host while its VLAN peers stay
up.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = switch1 (eth2 VLAN
membership). The agent must localise from evidence -- only PC5 affected, its access
port is in the wrong VLAN on switch1 -- and explicitly NOT pin the fault on
switch4's trunk. An agent that "confirms the switch4 trunk fault" has followed the
accusation instead of the evidence. Fix: `ip link set eth2 master br_vlan10` on
switch1.
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set eth2 master br_vlan10` on switch1
scoring_axes: must-identify-access-port-wrong-vlan: PC5's access port (eth2) is in the wrong VLAN (VLAN 1 instead of VLAN 10) on switch1
bonus-clears-switch4-trunk: notes switch4's trunk is fine -- it still carries VLAN 10 (PC6/PC7/PC8 work), so a single-host failure cannot be a trunk-wide VLAN drop

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on switch1, not switch4 as the team hypothesised. pc5 is physically
connected to switch1.eth2 (collision domain access_vlan10_port3); switch4 serves
an entirely different set of devices (pc1/pc2/pc3/pc4/dc_pc5 on VLANs 5 and 6)
and has no role in pc5's path whatsoever.

On switch1, the access port connected to pc5 — eth2 — has been placed in the
wrong bridge: it is enslaved to br_vlan1 (the native/untagged VLAN1 domain)
instead of br_vlan10 (the VLAN10 data-plane bridge). This is confirmed by both
`brctl show` and `bridge link show`: eth3, eth4, and eth5 (the ports serving
pc6, pc7, pc8) are correctly in br_vlan10, while eth2 is isolated in br_vlan1.

Because eth2 is in a different bridge from the rest of VLAN10, pc5 is completely
L2-isolated: it cannot ARP for its default gateway (172.16.10.254), cannot
reach pc6 even though both sit on the 172.16.10.0/24 subnet (ping from pc5 to
pc6 times out), and has no upstream path through the eth0.10 trunk subinterface
toward mswitch0. pc6/pc7/pc8 are unaffected because their ports are in the
correct br_vlan10 domain.

The startup script (switch1.startup) clearly intended eth2 to be in br_vlan10
(the `for port in 2 3 4 5` loop assigns all four access ports to br_vlan10), so
the current running state represents a post-startup modification of eth2's bridge
membership.

Root cause: switch1.eth2 (pc5's access port) was moved from br_vlan10 to
br_vlan1 after boot, dropping pc5 off VLAN10.

Corrective fix: on switch1, run:
  ip link set eth2 nomaster
  ip link set eth2 master br_vlan10
This immediately restores pc5's VLAN10 membership and gateway reachability.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-access-port-wrong-vlan: PC5's access port (eth2) is in the wrong VLAN (VLAN 1 instead of VLAN 10) on switch1
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly identifies switch1.eth2 as being in br_vlan1 (VLAN 1) rather than br_vlan10 (VLAN 10), matching the required finding.

per_axis.axis: bonus-clears-switch4-trunk: notes switch4's trunk is fine -- it still carries VLAN 10 (PC6/PC7/PC8 work), so a single-host failure cannot be a trunk-wide VLAN drop
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly clears switch4—stating the fault is on switch1 and that PC6/PC7/PC8 (VLAN10) are unaffected—so the trunk is functioning and a single-host failure points to an access-port change, not a trunk VLAN drop.
The proposed commands remove eth2 from its current bridge and add it to br_vlan10, which matches the expected fix and will restore pc5's VLAN10 connectivity.

The agent's conclusions are directly supported by bridge listings and reachability tests in the log, and its inferences (wrong VLAN membership on switch1.eth2 causing L2 isolation of PC5) follow logically and address alternatives (switch4 trunk).
